ns2:section.sectionText: "Race, Space, and (Post)Coloniality in Modern France" This interdisciplinary graduate course explores recent scholarly debates around race, space, and postcoloniality that have been transforming the study of France and the Francophone world. Drawing on historical, literary, and sociological perspectives, we will engage such topics as: race and racism in France and French thought; the formation and stigmatization of the "banlieues"; the histories and legacies of (post)colonial (im)migrations; and the reception of "postcolonial studies" in the French academy. (Taught in English; reading ability in French required)
